PullRequest.Title: Avoid synchronous activity bar size measurement
PullRequest.Body:
Remove the vertical activity bar's synchronous global-action-container `clientHeight` read during startup layout.

- Compute global action height from the rendered action count and the existing action-height/gap inputs that also drive CSS, including gaps only between items.
- Recompute available view-switcher space when Accounts is hidden or shown; keep repeated visibility updates idempotent.
- Preserve classic, compact, and Modern UI sizing, horizontal sidebar bars, and keyboard behavior. No CSS, labels, or keybindings change.

This follows the remaining activity-bar layout cost observed after the titlebar fix in #334751.

## Performance validation

Compared baseline and candidate on the same complete Code OSS development build at `333552ca38d5e15c8b734157159fcfcae9553c87`, using separate warmed profiles and alternating order. Baseline modules were compiled from HEAD using the repository's normal compiler; only the three affected generated modules were exchanged.

Five measured untraced launches and three measured traced launches per variant, after warmups:

| Startup metric (median) | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Activity-bar layout sampled self time | 26.094 ms | 0 ms |
| Total forced style/layout before `didStartWorkbench` | 26.850 ms | 14.936 ms |
| Untraced startup | 4,147 ms | 4,170 ms |
| Traced startup | 6,352 ms | 6,352 ms |

Forced layout decreases by approximately **44.4% (11.9 ms)** rather than merely disappearing from the original function's profile. A remaining flush occurs during focus handling.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A clientHeight geometry read of the rendered global action container ran synchronously inside every vertical Activity Bar layout, including the startup grid layout, and could flush pending style/layout work on the UI thread.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Main-thread startup and resize layout latency from synchronous browser style/layout resolution in ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Vertical Activity Bar layout computes reserved global-action height from the two-action in-memory count and static action height/gap inputs, avoiding the synchronous DOM geometry read during startup and later layouts while retaining a single arithmetic calculation per layout.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout synchronously read globalCompositeBar.element.clientHeight on every vertical layout. Workbench layout constructs the Activity Bar as a grid leaf and workbenchGrid.layout invokes part layout on startup; ActivitybarPart.layout then calls ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout. The global action bar has already appended rendered action DOM, so this geometry read sits on the synchronous main-thread startup/layout path and can require style/layout resolution. The changed code replaces that read with GlobalCompositeBar.getHeight(actionHeight, actionGap), which uses the in-memory ActionBar length and the same sizing values published to CSS. Tests explicitly install a throwing clientHeight getter and verify all supported size/gap combinations, corroborating that the DOM measurement is no longer reached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and subsequent vertical Activity Bar layout/resizes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench grid synchronously lays out the ActivitybarPart; ActivitybarPart.layout immediately calls ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout before the UI can finish the layout pass. The PR removes the global-action geometry read from this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Before the PR, reading globalCompositeBar.element.clientHeight crossed into browser style/layout resolution; the PR replaces it with an in-memory action-count calculation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One former geometry read per vertical Activity Bar layout, independent of view-container count; now zero reads for the global action bar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every vertical layout synchronously read the rendered global action container height.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The former read could synchronously flush pending style/layout on startup and every resize. The replacement arithmetic remains on the critical path but does not invoke browser geometry resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scales with the number of workbench layout passes (startup, window resize, and layout state changes), not with the number of activity items; global action cardinality is bounded at two.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread layout pass; no queue, limiter, or parallelism. Each grid layout invokes one Activity Bar layout, and the changed computation is O(1) because the global bar has one or two actions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Both cold and warm starts previously performed the geometry read; the changed path derives height directly on every call at constant cost.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the base changed line was a clientHeight read inside the synchronous layout method, and the new test proves the changed path does not access clientHeight.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact forced-layout duration depends on pending DOM/style invalidation and platform, but the synchronous geometry mechanism and startup reachability are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. This is a concrete performance fix, recorded separately with its blamed introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Showing or hiding the Accounts action from the Activity Bar preference
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A profile-storage change synchronously calls toggleAccountsActivity, which inserts or removes one ActionBar item, fires onDidChange, and performs one ActivityBarCompositeBar relayout when prior dimensions exist. The relayout computes global height in memory; only an independently configured compact menubar retains its pre-existing geometry read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Insert or remove the single Accounts DOM action and synchronously notify the owning composite bar to relayout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one DOM insertion/removal and one relayout per actual visibility transition; repeated same-state notifications are coalesced by the equality guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The DOM item was inserted or removed for each relevant storage event, but the owner was not immediately notified to recalculate available composite-bar space.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the user/storage-event path and completes before the visibility change returns; work is bounded to the two-item global bar.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: If compact menubar mode is enabled, relayout reads the existing menubar clientHeight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-existing menubar geometry read per triggered relayout; absent when compact menubar is not configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Account visibility changes did not directly invoke this layout method, though normal workbench layouts already used the same read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: May synchronously resolve layout on the rare account-visibility transition, but the new relayout is bounded and necessary to update available space; it is not a realistic hot-path regression.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Preference transitions, effectively one action among a maximum of two global actions; duplicate notifications with unchanged state do no work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous and serialized by the storage event delivery; idempotence suppresses duplicate relayouts when the preference already matches rendered state. One event affects one Activity Bar instance per window.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The preference is read from profile storage on each notification; no cache or network fetch is involved. The rendered-state guard acts as same-state coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added one-shot relayout and its bounded action count; low risk because duplicate events are suppressed and there is no collection or concurrency amplification.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Storage synchronization frequency across windows is environment-dependent, but normal interactive cardinality is low and each transition is bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous relayout occurs only on an actual rare visibility transition and prevents stale sizing; it does not create realistic repeated or scaling work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Horizontal Sidebar composite bar construction and layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SidebarPart creates ActivityBarCompositeBar with globalActivities undefined, so no GlobalCompositeBar, emitter subscription, height computation, or global-action DOM is created. Existing horizontal composite layout remains the only work on the path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing sidebar view-container count; the changed boolean-to-undefined constructor argument does not alter that cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-thread construction/layout, unchanged from before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes and no new cold/warm path distinction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both the old false value and new undefined value skip the global-activities branch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: constructor branching is directly visible and undefined preserves the prior false branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change and no finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and every diff page. The PR removes a synchronous global-action clientHeight read from startup/layout and adds only bounded, idempotent relayout work for account visibility changes. No actionable performance regression was introduced; the concrete synchronous-layout regression fix was recorded for learning.
